To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

consumers who are more attracted to online shopping than offline shopping perceive significantly lower channel risks, search effort, waiting (delivery) times, evaluation effort, but significantly higher price search intention, online than offline.
consumers are attracted to the Internet because it offers lower perceived risk, lower search effort, and lower waiting time.

the order of switching tendency is consistent with search and experience attributes; that consumers’ differences on channel risk perceptions, evaluation effort, waiting time between online/offline, and price search intentions significantly affect their channel-switching tendency; and that consumers attracted to online channels are more likely to perceive lower search cost, higher price search intentions, lower evaluation effort, and lower waiting time online than offline, whereas consumers attracted to offline are less likely to perceive these attributes online than offline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the consumer purchase decision-making process and its impact on channel switching.
the factors that affect consumer switching behavior from offline to online channels, which is a key issue in the development of e-commerce.
the purchase decision process and its impact on channel switching intentions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the purchase decision process characteristics, including channel risk perceptions, evaluation effort, search effort, waiting time, and price search intentions, are the key drivers of consumer channel switching intentions.
the operating characteristics of consumers’ purchase-decision processes have significant influences on their channel switching intentions.
the purchase decision process of consumers is the most important factor that influences their channel switching intentions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the consumer purchase-decision process is an important factor to consider when developing a successful online channel strategy.
consumers’ perceptions of the online shopping environment and their channel risk perceptions, search effort, and evaluation effort are the key determinants of their channel switching intentions.

the purchase decision process model is a good predictor of channel switching intentions and the model can be used as a basis to develop effective marketing strategies to attract consumers to purchase online.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumer channel switching can be better predicted by examining the operating characteristics of their purchase decision process.
consumer channel-switching behavior is not random but rather systematic, and it is influenced by their perceptions of channel attributes and their purchase decision processes.
the consumer purchase decision processes are important determinants of channel switching intentions.
